# Command-line reference (generated by scripts/make_cli_reference.py)

Every script is run from the bsce folder: `python scripts/<name>.py ...` (Spyder: `%run scripts/<name>.py ...`).
Scripts without options: `render_report.py` (VERIFICATION_REPORT.md -> .html), `summarize_tests.py` (test results -> tests/results/summary.md).

## aggregate_seeds.py

```
usage: aggregate_seeds.py [-h] --csv CSV

Mean +- std over training seeds from an evaluate.py result.

  python scripts/aggregate_seeds.py --csv outputs/SV_ULA/nmse_vs_snr.csv

Columns '<tag>' (seed 0, the normal run) and '<tag>_s1', '<tag>_s2', ... are one method trained
with different seeds (train.py --tag <tag>_s1 --set train.seed=1). Writes
nmse_vs_snr_seeds.csv (mean, std, n per method and SNR) and nmse_vs_snr_seeds.png (mean +- std,
values printed) next to the input.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --csv CSV
```

## check_3gpp.py

```
usage: check_3gpp.py [-h] [--raw RAW [RAW ...]]
                     [--builtin {UPA,ULA_Y,ULA} [{UPA,ULA_Y,ULA} ...]] [--n N]
                     [--spec {16.1,19.2}] [--channel {umi,umi_los,umi_nlos}]
                     [--element {38.901,omni}] [--seed SEED] [--n-test N_TEST]
                     [--n-cov N_COV] [--snr SNR [SNR ...]] [--no-transfer]
                     [--authors AUTHORS] [--name NAME] [--results RESULTS]

Check the 3GPP TR 38.901 channels of matlab/quadriga_make_H.m against the standard and compare them with SV and DeepMIMO.

  %run scripts/check_3gpp.py --builtin UPA ULA_Y              the built-in generator (as make_3gpp_data.py), 10,000 channels
  %run scripts/check_3gpp.py --raw UPA="raw3gpp/H_3gpp_upa_part*.mat" ULA_Y="raw3gpp/H_3gpp_ulay_part*.mat"
  (raw files of sionna_make_H.py / quadriga_make_H.m; ULA="..." adds the vertical ULA; KEY = UPA, ULA_Y or ULA)

1. LOS probability against 38.901 Table 7.4.2-1 (UMi street canyon), per 2-D distance bin.
2. The large-scale parameters drawn per user (DS, ASD, ASA, ZSD, ZSA, K) against 38.901 Table 7.5-6 (UMi street
   canyon) at the carrier of the files: median and robust log-std (IQR / 1.349), LOS and NLOS users apart. The spreads
   of the generated paths are shown too when the raw files have them (quadriga_make_H(..., 'realized', true)).
3. Beamspace x = U0^H h, ||x||^2 = N (as make_dataset.py): energy in the k strongest beams and the strongest-beam
   histogram, against bsce's SV and DeepMIMO test sets (data/SV_<ARR>, data/DeepMIMO_<ARR>).
4. Difficulty: NMSE of the LMMSE estimator built from the sample covariance of --n-cov training channels (the same
   number for every data set), on 2000 test channels, y = A(x + n), every data set with its own CS matrix.
5. Transfer: the authors' published GM-LAMP networks (trained on SV or DeepMIMO, reference/gmlamp/Train/Trained_Networks)
   on their own test set and on the 3GPP test set, at 5 dB (0-10 dB network) and 15 dB (10-20 dB network).
The 3GPP test set is the held-out-drop test set of make_dataset.py (the last --n-test users generated), its training
channels the first users. Writes results/<name>/check_3gpp.{json,md} and lsp_vs_38901.png, los_k_vs_38901.png,
beamspace_3datasets.png, beamspace_upa_maps.png, lmmse_3datasets.png, transfer_gmlamp.png.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --raw RAW [RAW ...]   KEY=pattern, KEY = UPA, ULA_Y or ULA
  --builtin {UPA,ULA_Y,ULA} [{UPA,ULA_Y,ULA} ...]
                        check the built-in generator (bsce/data/tr38901.py)
                        for these arrays instead of raw files
  --n N                 --builtin: channels per array
  --spec {16.1,19.2}    --builtin: 38.901 tables
  --channel {umi,umi_los,umi_nlos}
                        --builtin
  --element {38.901,omni}
                        --builtin
  --seed SEED           --builtin
  --n-test N_TEST
  --n-cov N_COV         training channels for the LMMSE sample covariance
  --snr SNR [SNR ...]
  --no-transfer         skip the GM-LAMP transfer test
  --authors AUTHORS
  --name NAME
  --results RESULTS
```

## check_combiners.py

```
usage: check_combiners.py [-h] --scenario SCENARIO --runs RUNS
                          [--tags [TAGS ...]] [--exclude [EXCLUDE ...]]
                          [--combiners [COMBINERS ...]]
                          [--combiner-files [COMBINER_FILES ...]]
                          [--classical CLASSICAL] [--graph-phase {own,target}]
                          [--n-test N_TEST] [--device DEVICE] [--out OUT]

Transfer check (v30): every network of a runs folder on a set of standard test combiners it never saw in training.

  %run scripts/check_combiners.py --scenario configs/scenarios/sv_ula.yaml --runs outputs/SV_ULA
  %run scripts/check_combiners.py --scenario configs/scenarios/sv_ula.yaml --runs outputs/SV_ULA --tags "G-LADMM*" GM-LAMP-authors
  %run scripts/check_combiners.py --scenario configs/scenarios/sv_ula.yaml --runs outputs/SV_ULA --combiners own pm1 dct M64
  %run scripts/check_combiners.py ... --combiner-files my_A1.mat my_A2.mat        (your own combiners, 'A' = M x N)

The test combiners (real M x N, N and M = M0 from the scenario; deterministic, written to <out>/combiners/):
  own        the scenario's combiner (the one the networks were trained with)
  pm1        random +-1/sqrt(M0), a new draw (seed 11)
  gauss      i.i.d. Gaussian / sqrt(M0)
  corr       Gaussian rows with correlation 0.9 between neighbouring RF chains (badly conditioned A A^T)
  sparse     partially connected: every RF chain sees 16 random beams (+-1/4), the rest 0
  dct        M0 random rows of the orthonormal DCT-II (a structured, deterministic transform subset)
  M<k>       random +-1/sqrt(k) with another number of RF chains: k = 1.25 M0, 0.75 M0, 0.5 M0 (160, 96, 64 for M0 = 128);
             in --combiners also by their aliases M+ M- M-- (whatever M0 is)
For every combiner, evaluate.py tests the networks on the scenario's test channels with the same noise:
  - networks that can follow a new combiner use it, any M: Graph-LADMM analytic, LADMM operator=analytic, and from v31
    NF-LADMM, LVAMP and ALISTA (nothing they learn depends on A);
  - the others keep the combiner they were learned for (that is the transfer test); with another M they cannot run.
  v31: a combiner on which evaluate.py fails, or where no method can run, is noted and the check goes on.
Writes <out>/ (default results/combiner_check_<SCENARIO>_<runs folder>):
  combiner_check.md / .csv   mean NMSE over the test SNRs, network x combiner, and the change against 'own'
  combiner_check.png         the same as a table, every value printed (red: worse than estimating zero)
  combiners.csv              M, cond(A A^T) and the mutual coherence of every test combiner
  <combiner>/                evaluate.py output (nmse_vs_snr.csv at every SNR, eval_log.json: who followed)
Options: --classical amp (default; '' = none), --graph-phase own|target (another data set's edge phases),
--n-test N (fewer test channels, quick look), --device.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenario SCENARIO
  --runs RUNS           runs folder, e.g. outputs/SV_ULA
  --tags [TAGS ...]     run folders (names or patterns); default: all
  --exclude [EXCLUDE ...]
  --combiners [COMBINERS ...]
                        subset of: own pm1 gauss corr sparse dct M+ M- M-- (or
                        the M<k> names; default: all)
  --combiner-files [COMBINER_FILES ...]
                        your own combiners (.mat with A, M x N)
  --classical CLASSICAL
  --graph-phase {own,target}
  --n-test N_TEST
  --device DEVICE
  --out OUT
```

## check_gm_components.py

```
usage: check_gm_components.py [-h] --runs RUNS [RUNS ...]

Which GM-LAMP networks still have identical mixture components (v31.1)?

  %run scripts/check_gm_components.py --runs "outputs/*"
  %run scripts/check_gm_components.py --runs outputs/SV_ULA/GM-LAMP-T8_paper_trscenario_precision-float32

GM-LAMP's original init gives its K mixture components identical values. Before bsce v31.1 they then got bit-identical
gradients in training and never separated. The mixture stayed one Gaussian: a denoiser that scales every entry by the
same factor and cannot use the sparsity. So the network stayed near the level of a linear estimator: about -2.9 dB after
the first layer on SV ULA at 10 dB, against -9.2 dB in the authors' training log.

Every GM-LAMP network trained with bsce before v31.1 from the original init is affected and has to be retrained:
gmlamp_original.yaml, run_suite.py --methods gmlamp, any protocol. These are not affected:
- networks trained with gm_init=spread (gmlamp_spread.yaml);
- the authors' published networks;
- the networks trained with v31.1.

Checked: every .pt file under the given run folders, with the layers whose theta_t has identical components. That
includes the checkpoints/ of an interrupted training: rerun its command with v31.1, which does not resume an affected
checkpoint but starts again. Exit code 1 when an affected network (not a checkpoint) is found.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --runs RUNS [RUNS ...]
                        run folders or patterns (e.g. 'outputs/*')
```

## check_vs_authors.py

```
usage: check_vs_authors.py [-h] [--scenarios SCENARIOS [SCENARIOS ...]]
                           [--runs [RUNS ...]] [--authors AUTHORS] [--no-data]
                           [--bootstrap BOOTSTRAP] [--name NAME]
                           [--results RESULTS]

Check the GM-LAMP data sets and the paper-protocol training of bsce against the authors' own files.

  %run scripts/check_vs_authors.py
  %run scripts/check_vs_authors.py --runs "outputs/*/GM-LAMP-T8_paper_trscenario" "outputs/*/LAMP-T8_paper_trscenario"

It needs reference/gmlamp (the authors' package, Wei-Hu-Dai 2021):
  CE_SV/CSmatrix256128.mat, CE_DeepMIMO/CSmatrix_128256.mat   the CS matrices of the two data sets
  Train/Trained_Networks/*.npz   the authors' training states: weights (identical to the published
                                 CE_*/Trained_*.mat used by Main.m) and the training log of every stage
and the data sets of scripts/make_gmlamp_data.py (data/SV_ULA, SV_UPA, DeepMIMO_ULA, DeepMIMO_UPA).

1. Measurement files (generate_measurement_data.py): the noise power of every chunk is estimated from y - A x with the
   authors' matrix of the data set. It must equal the stored SNR; training = 10 chunks with SNR in the band,
   validation = 10 dB.
2. Validation sets: the authors' 16 published networks on our validation set at 10 dB, against the validation NMSE the
   authors logged at the end of their training (their own validation set, also 10 dB). The difference is compared
   with the spread of a 2000-channel NMSE (bootstrap): |z| < 2 means "as close as two random validation sets".
3. --runs: a network retrained by bsce with the paper protocol (run_suite.py --protocol paper --train-snr scenario)
   against the authors' log of the same network (method, data set, band): the validation NMSE and the number of
   iterations of each of the 64 training stages.
Writes results/<name>/: authors_check.md, authors_check.json, validation_vs_authors.png, stages_<SCENARIO>_<run>_<band>.png.
The networks are computed with a NumPy port of the authors' TensorFlow graph (define_networks.build_LAMP), not with
bsce's models, so the check does not depend on the code it checks.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenarios SCENARIOS [SCENARIOS ...]
                        SV_ULA SV_UPA DeepMIMO_ULA DeepMIMO_UPA
  --runs [RUNS ...]     bsce LAMP / GM-LAMP run folders trained with the paper
                        protocol
  --authors AUTHORS     folder of the authors' .npz states
  --no-data             only the --runs comparison
  --bootstrap BOOTSTRAP
  --name NAME
  --results RESULTS
```

## compare.py

```
usage: compare.py [-h] --scenarios SCENARIOS [SCENARIOS ...]
                  [--tags [TAGS ...]] [--preset {ft,onenet}]
                  [--exclude [EXCLUDE ...]] [--best] [--ref REF]
                  [--no-authors] [--classical CLASSICAL]
                  [--classical-params CLASSICAL_PARAMS] [--no-cost]
                  [--name NAME] [--outputs OUTPUTS] [--results RESULTS]
                  [--device DEVICE] [--smoke] [--polish {none,band,snr}]
                  [--noise-model {colored,coloured,folded,white}]

Fair comparison of all trained networks: evaluation on the test set + figures + tables, in results/<name>/.

  %run scripts/compare.py --scenarios all
  %run scripts/compare.py --scenarios all 3gpp          (+ 3gpp_upa, 3gpp_ula: gains against a GM-LAMP trained here)
  %run scripts/compare.py --scenarios sv_upa deepmimo_upa --tags "*_ft_*" --name finetuned
  (fine-tuned folders: *_ft_* = the v24 names <run>_ft_<edges>dB_<k>; "*-ft" the v23 names, or scripts/rename_runs.py)
  %run scripts/compare.py --scenarios all --tags "LAMP-T8_paper_trscenario" "GM-LAMP-T8_paper_trscenario" --name paper_check

For every scenario:
  1. the authors' published GM-LAMP and LAMP networks are put in outputs/<SCENARIO>/ (GM-LAMP-authors, LAMP-authors)
     (import_gmlamp_weights.py; skipped with --no-authors or when the folders exist)
  2. every selected network is evaluated on the scenario's test set: the same 2000 test channels and the same noise
     realisation at every SNR for every method (evaluate.py)
Then, for all scenarios together:
  comparison.png / .pdf  one column per scenario: NMSE vs SNR, a table (0 / 10 / 20 dB, mean, gain over the reference,
                         parameters), the gain over the reference at every SNR (values printed)
  summary.csv            scenario, method, NMSE at every SNR, mean, gain over the reference, parameters, inference time,
                         v31: trained parameters (those that reach the output) and real MACs per channel (bsce/cost.py)
  summary.md / .tex      the table at 0 / 10 / 20 dB + mean + gain (paper-ready)
  networks.md            what every compared network is (method, T, protocol, data, bands), from its README / logs
  <SCENARIO>/            evaluate.py output (nmse_vs_snr.csv / .png, nmse_table.png, eval_log.json)

--tags        run folders to compare (names or glob patterns). Default: every folder in outputs/<SCENARIO>/
              (+ the authors' networks). The reference is always added.
--preset      (v30) the usual selections, the same as the workbench's: ft = every per-band fine-tune
              (*_ft_*, and *-ft of v23 and older); onenet = every one-network-0-20 dB run, whatever its suffix
              (G-LADMM-T8_paper, LADMM-T6_fair, ...), without fine-tunes, other training ranges and ensembles.
              --tags and --exclude add to it.
--ref         reference for the gains (default GM-LAMP-authors)
--classical   classical baselines evaluated as well (default amp; also omp, sd; v31: l1, grwl1 tuned per SNR by
              scripts/tune_classical.py, --classical-params)
--noise-model white   the networks trained with white noise (outputs/<SCENARIO>_white/, run_suite --noise-model white),
              tested with white noise. The published GM-LAMP / LAMP were trained with colored noise, so they are not
              imported there: the reference is then a GM-LAMP trained here with white noise (--ref to change it).
              Both noise models side by side, with cross tests: scripts/compare_noise.py.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenarios SCENARIOS [SCENARIOS ...]
  --tags [TAGS ...]
  --preset {ft,onenet}  ft: every fine-tune; onenet: every one-network-0-20 dB
                        run (any suffix); adds to --tags
  --exclude [EXCLUDE ...]
                        leave out the run folders matching these patterns,
                        e.g. '*_ft_*' (passed to evaluate.py)
  --best                v31.3: every method in its best configuration: leave
                        out the variants that run_suite.py --warm-start best
                        did not choose
                        (outputs/<SCENARIO>/best_warm_start.json)
  --ref REF
  --no-authors
  --classical CLASSICAL
  --classical-params CLASSICAL_PARAMS
                        v31: for --classical l1 / grwl1, the tune_classical.py
                        file of every scenario (<SCENARIO> is replaced by the
                        scenario name)
  --no-cost             v31: leave out the trained-parameter and MACs-per-
                        channel columns (bsce/cost.py)
  --name NAME
  --outputs OUTPUTS
  --results RESULTS
  --device DEVICE
  --smoke
  --polish {none,band,snr}
                        v28: also every network + least squares on its
                        strongest beams ('<run>+polish' columns; passed to
                        evaluate.py)
  --noise-model {colored,coloured,folded,white}
                        colored (default): outputs/<SCENARIO>/ on colored test
                        noise; white: outputs/<SCENARIO>_white/ on white test
                        noise
```

## compare_noise.py

```
usage: compare_noise.py [-h] --scenarios SCENARIOS [SCENARIOS ...]
                        [--tags [TAGS ...]] [--exclude [EXCLUDE ...]]
                        [--nf-matched] [--no-authors] [--classical CLASSICAL]
                        [--name NAME] [--outputs OUTPUTS] [--results RESULTS]
                        [--device DEVICE] [--smoke]

Colored against white measurement noise: every network on both test noises, trained on either (cross tests).

  %run scripts/compare_noise.py --scenarios sv_ula --tags NF-LADMM-S-T8 LADMM-T6-ft GM-LAMP-T8-ft
  %run scripts/compare_noise.py --scenarios sv_ula sv_upa --tags "NF-LADMM*" --nf-matched --name noise_nf

Needs the networks trained with both noise models under the same names:
  outputs/<SCENARIO>/<tag>          run_suite.py ...                        (colored, y = A (x + n), the default)
  outputs/<SCENARIO>_white/<tag>    run_suite.py ... --noise-model white    (white, y = A x + w, same mean noise power)
(a tag present in one folder only is still shown, for the noise model it has). The authors' published GM-LAMP and LAMP
(trained with colored noise) are added from outputs/<SCENARIO>/ for SV / DeepMIMO (import_gmlamp_weights.py if missing;
--no-authors to leave them out).

For every scenario and test noise (colored, white), with the same 2000 test channels and the same noise draw (the white
test noise is the colored draw whitened, bsce/data/noise.py), evaluate.py is run on both folders:
  trained on the test's noise model  -> solid line ("matched training")
  trained on the other noise model   -> dashed line ("cross": what a network loses when the noise model changes)
  --nf-matched: NF-LADMM networks of the other folder once more with the exact data step of the test noise (same
                weights, evaluate.py --nf-step matched) -> dotted line
Writes results/<name>/:
  noise_comparison.png / .pdf  one row per scenario: NMSE vs SNR on colored | on white test noise (value at the last
                               SNR next to each line) | mismatch loss at every SNR (cross - matched training, dB)
  noise_summary.csv / .md      every line: method, trained on, data step, tested on, NMSE at every SNR, mean
  <SCENARIO>/train-<a>_test-<b>[_nfmatched]/   the evaluate.py outputs

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenarios SCENARIOS [SCENARIOS ...]
  --tags [TAGS ...]     run folders (names or patterns); default: all
  --exclude [EXCLUDE ...]
                        leave out the run folders matching these patterns
  --nf-matched          also NF-LADMM trained on the other noise with the
                        exact data step of the test noise
  --no-authors
  --classical CLASSICAL
  --name NAME
  --outputs OUTPUTS
  --results RESULTS
  --device DEVICE
  --smoke
```

## compare_variants.py

```
usage: compare_variants.py [-h] --scenarios SCENARIOS [SCENARIOS ...]
                           --variants VARIANTS [VARIANTS ...] [--train TRAIN]
                           [--protocol PROTOCOL] [--set [SET ...]]
                           [--seeds SEEDS [SEEDS ...]] [--device DEVICE]
                           [--out OUT] [--skip-train] [--refs [REFS ...]]

Train model variants under one protocol on several scenarios, evaluate them on the same test
data and plot the comparison.

  python scripts/compare_variants.py --scenarios q1k_sv_upa q1k_sv_ula       --variants scalar:model.threshold=scalar group:model.threshold=group group_k:model.threshold=group_k       --set model.T=2 train.maxit=1000 train.better_wait=100000000 model.precision=float32 model.init_precision=float32       --protocol gmlamp_best --out outputs_cmp --seeds 0

Every variant 'name:override ...' (overrides separated by ',') is trained with train.py (--tag LADMM-<name>[_s<k>]),
then evaluate.py runs on outputs_cmp/<scenario>/ (same test channels and noise for all), and
compare.png / compare.csv / compare.json summarise NMSE vs SNR and the difference to the first
variant (mean over seeds when several).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenarios SCENARIOS [SCENARIOS ...]
                        names in configs/scenarios (without .yaml)
  --variants VARIANTS [VARIANTS ...]
  --train TRAIN
  --protocol PROTOCOL
  --set [SET ...]
  --seeds SEEDS [SEEDS ...]
  --device DEVICE
  --out OUT
  --skip-train
  --refs [REFS ...]     other model folders in the runs folder to draw as
                        references (e.g. LAMP-authors GM-LAMP-authors)
```

## deepmimo_convert.py

```
usage: deepmimo_convert.py [-h] --scenario SCENARIO --input INPUT [INPUT ...]
                           [--var VAR] [--n-train N_TRAIN] [--n-val N_VAL]
                           [--n-test N_TEST] [--lens {gmlamp,bsce}] [--conj]
                           [--upa-order {as_is,transpose}]
                           [--test {reference,random}] [--reference REFERENCE]
                           [--set [SET ...]]

Turn raw DeepMIMO spatial channels h into GM-LAMP's beamspace data sets.

  python scripts/deepmimo_convert.py --scenario configs/scenarios/deepmimo_upa.yaml --input H_upa.mat
  then:  python scripts/generate_data.py --scenario configs/scenarios/deepmimo_upa.yaml --measurements-only

Raw channels: matlab/deepmimo_make_H.m (DeepMIMO v1.3, O1_28, BS 3, rows 1000-1300, 3 paths,
1 subcarrier; ULA = 256 elements on the z axis, UPA = 16 x 16 on the y, z axes).

GM-LAMP's beamspace convention for DeepMIMO (identified on its CE_DeepMIMO test files: every one
of its 2000 UPA test channels is found among these users with complex fidelity ~1 - 4e-11):
    x = U0^H h,   U0(n, k) = exp(j 2 pi n (k - (N-1)/2) / N) / sqrt(N),  n, k = 0..N-1
(element index from 0, symmetric beam grid; UPA: kron(U0_16, U0_16) on DeepMIMO's element order),
then ||x||^2 = N per channel. This differs from the SV lens matrix (centred element index), so
--lens gmlamp (default) is required to obtain GM-LAMP's data; --lens bsce gives x = U.' h.

Split (--test reference, default): the test set is GM-LAMP's own test file (identical channels),
its users are removed from the pool, and training / validation are drawn (seeded) from the rest:
50000 / 2000. --test random draws all three sets from the pool.
Outputs (data_dir): DeepMIMO_<ARR>_{training,validation,test}_channel.mat (x, N x K),
deepmimo_stats.json (match with GM-LAMP, statistics), deepmimo_stats.png.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenario SCENARIO
  --input INPUT [INPUT ...]
                        .mat file(s) with raw channels h
  --var VAR             variable name (default: largest complex array)
  --n-train N_TRAIN     default: scenario n_train or 50000
  --n-val N_VAL         default: scenario n_val or 2000
  --n-test N_TEST       default: scenario n_test or 2000 (--test random)
  --lens {gmlamp,bsce}  gmlamp: x = U0^H h (GM-LAMP's DeepMIMO data); bsce: x
                        = U.' h (SV lens matrix)
  --conj                --lens bsce only: use conj(h)
  --upa-order {as_is,transpose}
  --test {reference,random}
                        reference: test set = GM-LAMP's test file, its users
                        excluded from training
  --reference REFERENCE
                        GM-LAMP beamspace test file (default
                        reference/gmlamp/CE_DeepMIMO/<ARR>_test_channel.mat)
  --set [SET ...]
```

## depth_curve.py

```
usage: depth_curve.py [-h] --runs RUNS [RUNS ...] [--tol TOL] [--out OUT]

NMSE versus number of layers from layer-wise training logs, and the recommended depth T.

  python scripts/depth_curve.py --runs outputs/SV_ULA/LADMM-full_gmlamp outputs/SV_UPA/LADMM-full_gmlamp
  options: --tol 0.1   recommended T = smallest depth within tol dB of the best depth, in every band
           --out <dir> (default: outputs/depth_curve)

With layer-wise training, the validation NMSE of the t-layer network is logged when layer t is
finished (with its refinements). One run with model.T=12 therefore gives the whole depth curve.
The shallow prefixes of the FINAL model are not usable estimators (later refinements retune the
early layers for the last output), so the curve uses the logged values; the network with the
chosen T is trained afresh in S3. Writes depth_curve.png (values printed),
depth_curve.csv and depth_curve.json (recommended T per run and overall).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --runs RUNS [RUNS ...]
                        run folders containing train_log.json
  --tol TOL
  --out OUT
```

## depth_snapshots.py

```
usage: depth_snapshots.py [-h] --runs RUNS [RUNS ...] [--band BAND]
                          [--tol TOL] [--snr SNR [SNR ...]] [--device DEVICE]
                          [--out OUT] [--name NAME]

Depth curve on the TEST set: NMSE of the network saved when each layer was finished (train.py --save-layers).

  python scripts/depth_snapshots.py --runs outputs/DeepMIMO_UPA/LADMM-best-T12 outputs/DeepMIMO_ULA/LADMM-best-T12
  python scripts/depth_snapshots.py --runs "outputs/*/LADMM-T12" "outputs/*/LAMP-T16" --name depth_ladmm_lamp
  (--runs accepts patterns: * matches any scenario or name; every match that has a layers/ folder is used)
  options: --band 0to20dB (default: the only/first band found)   --tol 0.1 (dB, "flat" threshold)
           --snr 0 10 20 (SNRs drawn as curves; the mean is over all test SNRs of the scenario)
           --device auto   --name depth (results/<name>/)   --out <dir> (instead of results/<name>)

For every run folder: reads <run>/layers/T<t>_<tag>_<band>.pt and the scenario stored in <run>/train_log.json,
evaluates every T on the scenario's test channels with exactly the noise of evaluate.py
(NumpyMatlabRNG(seed + 1000 + i) at test SNR i; white for a run trained with --noise-model white), and writes
  depth_curve.png / .pdf   one column per run: (top) test NMSE vs T at the chosen SNRs + the mean over all test SNRs,
                           (bottom) validation NMSE logged when layer T was finished + gain of each added layer
  depth_curve.csv          run, T, n_params, validation, test NMSE at every SNR, mean
  depth_curve.md           the same as a table, with the flat point of every run
Flat point (v31.3): the smallest T whose VALIDATION NMSE is within --tol dB of the best T of that run. The depth is
chosen on validation data, never on the test set; the test curves are shown for the record only.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --runs RUNS [RUNS ...]
  --band BAND
  --tol TOL
  --snr SNR [SNR ...]
  --device DEVICE
  --out OUT
  --name NAME
```

## evaluate.py

```
usage: evaluate.py [-h] --scenario SCENARIO --runs RUNS
                   [--classical CLASSICAL] [--admm-lambdas ADMM_LAMBDAS]
                   [--classical-params CLASSICAL_PARAMS] [--device DEVICE]
                   [--n-test N_TEST] [--out OUT] [--tags [TAGS ...]]
                   [--exclude [EXCLUDE ...]]
                   [--noise-model {auto,colored,coloured,folded,white}]
                   [--polish {none,band,snr}] [--polish-n-val POLISH_N_VAL]
                   [--combiner COMBINER] [--graph-phase {own,target}]
                   [--nf-step {trained,matched}]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenario SCENARIO
  --runs RUNS
  --classical CLASSICAL
  --admm-lambdas ADMM_LAMBDAS
                        .mat with 'lambdas' (one per test SNR)
  --classical-params CLASSICAL_PARAMS
                        v31: JSON of scripts/tune_classical.py (lam and eps
                        per test SNR) for --classical l1 / grwl1
  --device DEVICE
  --n-test N_TEST
  --out OUT
  --tags [TAGS ...]     only these run folders (names or glob patterns, e.g.
                        '*-ft' 'GM-LAMP-authors')
  --exclude [EXCLUDE ...]
                        leave out the run folders matching these names or
                        patterns (after --tags), e.g. '*_ft_*'
  --noise-model {auto,colored,coloured,folded,white}
                        test noise: auto (default) = white for a runs folder
                        <scenario>_white, else the scenario's noise_model
                        (colored); colored = y = A (x + n); white = y = A x +
                        w (same draw, whitened)
  --polish {none,band,snr}
                        v28: also evaluate every network + least squares on
                        its K strongest beams (columns '<run>+polish'); K, eps
                        chosen on validation channels per band (band) or per
                        test SNR (snr)
  --polish-n-val POLISH_N_VAL
                        validation channels for the polish choice (default
                        all)
  --combiner COMBINER   v29: test with another combiner: a .mat file with A (M
                        x N), or random:<seed>[:<M>] (+-1/sqrt(M); v30: :<M>
                        gives another number of RF chains, e.g. random:11:64)
  --graph-phase {own,target}
                        v29: Graph-LADMM edge phases: own (as trained) or
                        target (estimated from this data set)
  --nf-step {trained,matched}
                        NF-LADMM data step: trained (default) = the noise
                        model the network was trained with; matched = the
                        exact step of the test noise model (same weights, no
                        retraining)
```

## finetune_bands.py

```
usage: finetune_bands.py [-h] [--scenario SCENARIO] --from SRC [--tag TAG]
                         [--bands BANDS] [--snr SNR [SNR ...]]
                         [--val {range,file}]
                         [--val-snr VAL_SNR [VAL_SNR ...]] [--margin MARGIN]
                         [--iters ITERS] [--batch BATCH] [--lr LR] [--lr2 LR2]
                         [--lr2-frac LR2_FRAC] [--val-every VAL_EVERY]
                         [--seed SEED] [--grad-clip GRAD_CLIP]
                         [--device DEVICE]
                         [--noise-model {colored,coloured,folded,white}]
                         [--out OUT] [--patience PATIENCE]
                         [--min-gain MIN_GAIN] [--snr-dist {chunks,fair}]
                         [--combiner {auto,fixed,random}]
                         [--snr-step SNR_STEP]
                         [--checkpoint-minutes CHECKPOINT_MINUTES]
                         [--dry-name]

Fine-tune a trained network per SNR band (by default 0-10 and 10-20 dB), next to it, with a clear name; resumable.

  %run scripts/finetune_bands.py --from outputs/SV_UPA/LADMM-T6
      -> outputs/SV_UPA/LADMM-T6_ft_0-10-20dB_20k/LADMM-T6_ft_0-10-20dB_20k_0to10dB.pt and ..._10to20dB.pt
  %run scripts/finetune_bands.py --from outputs/SV_UPA/LADMM-T6 --snr 0 5 10 15 20 --iters 10000
      -> outputs/SV_UPA/LADMM-T6_ft_0-5-10-15-20dB_10k/  (four bands)
  %run scripts/finetune_bands.py --from Trained_LADMM_for_SV_UPA_2561280to20dB_1_11dB_better.pt --scenario sv_upa_user_2band

--from     a run folder (its one network file is used) or a .pt file (also an untitled2.py checkpoint, or a depth
           snapshot <run>/layers/T06_<run>_<band>.pt: its scenario comes from <run>/train_log.json and the fine-tune is
           named <run>_T06_ft_..., next to <run>)
--snr      band edges (default 0 10 20; or the scenario's bands with --snr scenario)
--iters    iterations per band (default 20000, as run_suite.py)
Name:      <source folder>_ft_<edges>dB_<iterations>[_<option>...], in the source's folder (outputs/<SCENARIO>/):
           the options that differ from the defaults are added (_margin2, _val10, _clip1, _lr0p0001, _batch256, _seed1 ...: a dot becomes p),
           so another setting never overwrites a fine-tune. --tag NAME to choose the name; --dry-name prints the name.
Early stop: a learning rate ends when the best validation has not improved by --min-gain dB (0.01) during --patience
           steps (4000): the first rate then hands over to the second, and the second ends the band. The best validated
           state is kept as before. --patience 0 = always the whole --iters (as up to v24).
Resume:    the same command again continues an interrupted fine-tune: finished bands are kept, the band that was
           running continues from its last checkpoint (every --checkpoint-minutes, default 10), exactly as if it had
           not stopped. A folder made with other settings or from another version of the source is never mixed in:
           the script stops and says so.
--scenario may be left out: the scenario stored in the source's train_log.json is used (the data the network was
           trained on, also its noise model). Other options: --val range|file, --val-snr 10, --margin 2, --batch 400,
           --lr 5e-5, --lr2 5e-6, --lr2-frac 0.3333, --val-every 100, --seed 0, --grad-clip, --bands 0to10dB,
           --noise-model, --out <parent folder>, --device auto.
--snr-dist fair (v26): the SNRs of every minibatch spread evenly over the band (one in each of `batch` equal parts,
           random order) instead of i.i.d. U(band); --snr-step 0.2: on the grid lo, lo+0.2, ..., hi. The validation
           (--val range) is then at 100 equally spaced SNRs of the band instead of random ones. Suffix _fair / _fair0p2.

Per band (each starts from the same source network):
  * all parameters, torch Adam; lr for the first (1-lr2_frac)*iters steps, then lr2 (restarted from the best state)
    = untitled2.py's last two refinement rates (0.1 and 0.01 x 5e-4)
  * minibatch: `batch` training channels drawn with replacement + FRESH noise each step, one SNR per sample ~ U(band.train)
  * validation every `val-every` steps on the validation channels with fixed noise, SNR ~ U(band) (seed 123)
    (--val file: the band's validation measurement file instead, when it exists);
    pooled linear NMSE; the best validated state is kept
Output: <folder>/<folder>_<band>.pt/.mat (+ _orig.mat), finetune_log.json, README.txt -> evaluate.py uses the set.
On SV UPA the fine-tune of the user's untitled2.py 0-20 dB network gave the best LADMM of 14 Oct (LADMM_why_0to20_SV.md).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenario SCENARIO   scenario name (sv_upa) or yaml; default: the one
                        stored in train_log.json next to --from
  --from SRC            a run folder (outputs/SV_UPA/LADMM-T6) or a .pt file
  --tag TAG             folder name; default:
                        <source>_ft_<edges>dB_<iterations>[_<options>]
  --bands BANDS
  --snr SNR [SNR ...]   band edges: '0 10 20' (default) -> 0to10dB, 10to20dB;
                        '0 5 10 15 20' -> four bands; 'scenario' = the
                        scenario's bands
  --val {range,file}    range (default): validation = validation channels +
                        fixed noise, SNR ~ U(band) (seed 123); file: the
                        band's validation measurement file if it exists (GM-
                        LAMP's files are at 10 dB only)
  --val-snr VAL_SNR [VAL_SNR ...]
                        validation at fixed SNRs instead of --val: e.g. '10'
                        (as the authors: 10 dB for both bands) or '0 5 10';
                        equal chunks, fixed noise (seed 123)
  --margin MARGIN       edge margin in dB: training noise SNR ~ U(lo - M, hi +
                        M) for the band [lo, hi]; validation stays on the band
                        (default 0)
  --iters ITERS         iterations per band (default 20000)
  --batch BATCH
  --lr LR
  --lr2 LR2
  --lr2-frac LR2_FRAC
  --val-every VAL_EVERY
  --seed SEED
  --grad-clip GRAD_CLIP
                        clip the global gradient norm at this value (default:
                        no clipping, as before)
  --device DEVICE
  --noise-model {colored,coloured,folded,white}
                        measurement noise of the fine-tune (default: the one
                        the network was trained with)
  --out OUT             parent folder of the result; default: the folder that
                        holds the source network's folder
                        (outputs/<scenario>/), so the fine-tuned networks sit
                        next to their source
  --patience PATIENCE   early stop: when the best validation has not improved
                        by --min-gain dB during this many steps, the first
                        learning rate ends (the second starts), and in the
                        second the band ends (default 4000; 0 = always the
                        whole --iters)
  --min-gain MIN_GAIN   the gain (dB) that counts for --patience (default
                        0.01)
  --snr-dist {chunks,fair}
                        SNRs of the minibatches: chunks (default, as before:
                        i.i.d. U(band) per sample) or fair: spread evenly over
                        the band in every minibatch; the validation then at
                        equally spaced SNRs (suffix _fair)
  --combiner {auto,fixed,random}
                        v29: random = a new random +-1/sqrt(M) combiner every
                        step (networks that follow the combiner: Graph-LADMM
                        analytic, analytic LADMM); auto (default) = random
                        when the source was trained with
                        train.combiner=random, else fixed (the scenario's
                        combiner)
  --snr-step SNR_STEP   with --snr-dist fair: SNRs on the grid lo, lo+STEP,
                        ..., hi (suffix _fair<step>)
  --checkpoint-minutes CHECKPOINT_MINUTES
                        save the band being trained every this many minutes
                        (resume point; 0 = never)
  --dry-name            print the folder the fine-tune would write, then stop
```

## make_3gpp_data.py

```
usage: make_3gpp_data.py [-h] [--sizes {sv,deepmimo,dong2019,100k}]
                         [--n-train N_TRAIN] [--n-val N_VAL] [--n-test N_TEST]
                         [--only ONLY] [--spec {16.1,19.2}]
                         [--channel {umi,umi_los,umi_nlos}]
                         [--element {38.901,omni}] [--snr SNR [SNR ...]]
                         [--suffix SUFFIX] [--seed SEED]
                         [--drop-users DROP_USERS] [--out-root OUT_ROOT]
                         [--check] [--force] [--dry-run]

Make the 3GPP TR 38.901 data sets of bsce in ONE command (as make_gmlamp_data.py does for SV and DeepMIMO).

  %run scripts/make_3gpp_data.py                          3GPP_UPA and 3GPP_ULA, 80,000 / 2,000 / 2,000 (the sizes of SV)
  %run scripts/make_3gpp_data.py --sizes dong2019         81,000 / 9,000 / 19,000 (Dong et al., IEEE JSTSP 2019)
  %run scripts/make_3gpp_data.py --n-train 96000 --n-val 2000 --n-test 2000
  %run scripts/make_3gpp_data.py --only 3GPP_ULAZ         the vertical ULA (the geometry of GM-LAMP's DeepMIMO ULA)
  %run scripts/make_3gpp_data.py --spec 19.2 --suffix _v19         a second copy with the Rel-19 tables
  options: --check (statistics against 38.901 and against SV / DeepMIMO afterwards)  --force  --dry-run

What is made (configs/scenarios/3gpp_upa.yaml, 3gpp_ula.yaml, 3gpp_ulaz.yaml; data/<NAME>/), Python only:
  channels     3GPP TR 38.901 v16.1 (--spec 19.2: Rel-19 tables), UMi street canyon, LOS/NLOS by Table 7.4.2-1, 28 GHz,
               narrowband, plane waves; BS at 10 m, single-polarised 38.901 elements, lambda/2. 3GPP_UPA: UPA 16 x 16 on
               y-z; 3GPP_ULA: ULA 256 on y (horizontal); 3GPP_ULAZ: ULA 256 on z (vertical). One isotropic UE antenna
               at 1.5 m, users uniform in the 120-degree hexagonal sector (ISD 200 m, d2D >= 10 m), outdoor.
               Built-in generator bsce/data/tr38901.py: the TR procedure as written, checked against Sionna 2.2
               (docs/3GPP_DATASET.md)
  beamspace    x = U0^H h (the DeepMIMO convention), ||x||^2 = N per channel
  split        training / validation / test from separate drops (no drop shared); the validation and test users are
               the same for any size, and the same users for the three arrays (fixed seeds)
  measurements as GM-LAMP's: y = A (x + n), A = CSmatrix256128; bands 0-10 and 10-20 dB, 10 SNR chunks per training
               file, validation at 10 dB (--snr <edges> for other bands)
  files        <D>_<ARR>_{training,validation,test}_channel.mat (x, N x K), the measurement files, CSmatrix.mat,
               <D>_<ARR>_meta.mat (position, LOS state, drop, large-scale parameters of every channel),
               dataset_info.json, dataset_check.png: the format of data/SV_* and data/DeepMIMO_*
Train as the other scenarios: run_suite.py --scenarios 3gpp_upa 3gpp_ula ... (or --scenarios all 3gpp).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --sizes {sv,deepmimo,dong2019,100k}
                        (train, val, test): sv 80000/2000/2000, deepmimo
                        50000/2000/2000, dong2019 81000/9000/19000, 100k
                        96000/2000/2000
  --n-train N_TRAIN     exact sizes instead of --sizes (all three)
  --n-val N_VAL
  --n-test N_TEST
  --only ONLY           comma list of 3GPP_UPA, 3GPP_ULA, 3GPP_ULAZ
  --spec {16.1,19.2}
  --channel {umi,umi_los,umi_nlos}
  --element {38.901,omni}
  --snr SNR [SNR ...]   band edges instead of the authors' bands
  --suffix SUFFIX       e.g. _v19: data/3GPP_UPA_v19 and
                        configs/scenarios/3gpp_upa_v19.yaml
  --seed SEED
  --drop-users DROP_USERS
  --out-root OUT_ROOT
  --check               afterwards: check_3gpp.py --builtin (10,000 channels)
  --force               overwrite existing data sets
  --dry-run             print the commands only
```

```
ONE command per data set: channels (train / val / test) + measurement files for any SNR bands + a scenario file.

SV (Python only, ~1 min for 200k):

DeepMIMO (after MATLAB has written the raw channels H, see matlab/deepmimo_make_H_chunks.m):

         (built-in generator, Python only, ~1.5 min per 100k)

         --n-val 2000 --n-test 2000 --authors-bands --name 3GPP_UPA_100k
         (raw channels of scripts/sionna_make_H.py or matlab/quadriga_make_H.m instead)

Options
  --n 200000 --split 0.90 0.05 0.05     total number of channels and train/val/test fractions (default 0.90/0.05/0.05)
  --n-train / --n-val / --n-test         exact sizes instead (override --n/--split)
  --sizes sv|deepmimo|dong2019|100k      a preset of (train, val, test): sv 80000/2000/2000 (GM-LAMP's SV), deepmimo
                                         50000/2000/2000 (GM-LAMP's DeepMIMO), dong2019 81000/9000/19000 (Dong et al.,
                                         IEEE JSTSP 2019: 3GPP TR 38.901 CDL, 28 GHz), 100k 96000/2000/2000
  --test standard|random                 standard (default): the 2000 test channels every bsce/GM-LAMP result uses
                                         (SV: bsce's SV test set; DeepMIMO: GM-LAMP's CE_DeepMIMO test file, whose users
                                         are removed from train/val) -> results comparable with the paper tables.
                                         3GPP: held-out drops (no drop shared between the sets). Built-in generator:
                                         the test users are the same for any --n-train / --n-val (fixed drops).
                                         random: a fresh test split of size n_test from the same pool
  --snr 0 20 | 0 10 20 | -5 0 10 20 30   SNR band edges (dB): one measurement file pair (train + val) per band,
                                         100 SNR chunks ~ U(band); the SNR of every column is stored ('snr_db')
  --authors-bands                        instead of --snr: the bands of sv_*.yaml / deepmimo_*.yaml (GM-LAMP's protocol):
                                         0-10 and 10-20 dB, 10 SNR chunks per training file, validation at 10 dB
  --no-measurements                      channels only (train later with --noise online, or add bands later with
                                         scripts/make_sv_measurements.py --scenario <written yaml> --snr ...)
  --test-measurements                    also write test measurement files at the scenario's test SNRs (0:2:20 dB), with
                                         exactly the noise evaluate.py uses (for MATLAB tests)
  --noise-model colored|white|both       measurement noise of the files: colored y = A (x + n) (default), white
                                         y = A x + w (files <name>_white.mat, used by --noise-model white runs), or both
                                         (paired: the white files are the colored ones with the same draw whitened)
  --seed 2026  --out-dir data/<name>  --force
3GPP with the built-in generator (no --input; bsce/data/tr38901.py, the TR 38.901 procedure as written):
  --ula-axis y|z                         ULA on y (horizontal, default) or z (vertical, the geometry of GM-LAMP's
                                         DeepMIMO ULA); the UPA is 16 x 16 on y-z
  --spec 16.1|19.2  --channel umi|umi_los|umi_nlos  --element 38.901|omni  --drop-users 250
  --raw-out PREFIX                       also write the raw channels (<PREFIX>_part001.mat, ...; check_3gpp.py --raw)

Writes data/<name>/
  <D>_<ARR>_{training,validation,test}_channel.mat     x (N x K), ||x||^2 = N on average (SV) / exactly (DeepMIMO)
  <D>_<ARR>_{training,validation}_128_measurements_<band>.mat    y (M x K) + snr_db (1 x K)
  CSmatrix.mat (GM-LAMP's A: CSmatrix256128 for SV and 3GPP, CSmatrix_128256 for DeepMIMO), dataset_info.json,
  dataset_check.png
and configs/scenarios/<name lower case>.yaml -> train with
  python scripts/train.py --scenario configs/scenarios/<name>.yaml --train configs/train/ladmm_best.yaml
(add --snr <edges> to train other bands than the ones made here; missing files are then made automatically).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dataset {SV,DeepMIMO,3GPP}
  --array {ULA,UPA}
  --n N
  --split SPLIT SPLIT SPLIT
  --n-train N_TRAIN
  --n-val N_VAL
  --n-test N_TEST
  --sizes {sv,deepmimo,dong2019,100k}
                        (train, val, test) preset: sv 80000/2000/2000,
                        deepmimo 50000/2000/2000, dong2019 81000/9000/19000,
                        100k 96000/2000/2000
  --test {standard,random}
  --snr SNR [SNR ...]
  --authors-bands       bands 0-10 / 10-20 dB, 10 SNR chunks, validation at 10
                        dB (sv_*.yaml, deepmimo_*.yaml)
  --no-measurements
  --test-measurements
  --noise-model {colored,white,both}
                        measurement files: colored y = A (x + n) (default, as
                        GM-LAMP), white y = A x + w (files <name>_white.mat),
                        or both (the white files are the colored ones with the
                        same noise draw whitened, so the two sets are paired;
                        bsce/data/noise.py)
  --input INPUT [INPUT ...]
                        DeepMIMO / 3GPP: raw channel .mat files (wildcards
                        allowed)
  --name NAME
  --out-dir OUT_DIR
  --seed SEED
  --force

3GPP, built-in generator (no --input):
  --ula-axis {y,z}      ULA on y (horizontal) or z (vertical)
  --spec {16.1,19.2}    38.901 tables
  --channel {umi,umi_los,umi_nlos}
                        LOS/NLOS by Table 7.4.2-1, or all LOS / all NLOS
  --element {38.901,omni}
                        BS element
  --drop-users DROP_USERS
                        users per drop
  --raw-out RAW_OUT     also write the raw channels to <PREFIX>_part001.mat,
                        ...
```

## make_ensemble.py

```
usage: make_ensemble.py [-h] --runs RUNS [RUNS ...] --tag TAG [--out OUT]

Put separately trained networks together into one model-averaging ensemble (UTRR-E: Wu, Cheng, Eldar, Cioffi,
IEEE TCOM 2025, Sec. IV-D): xhat = mean of the members' outputs.

  %run scripts/make_ensemble.py --runs outputs/SV_ULA/UTRR-T30_paper_K-0 outputs/SV_ULA/UTRR-T30_paper outputs/SV_ULA/UTRR-T30_paper_K-64 outputs/SV_ULA/UTRR-T30_paper_K-256 --tag UTRR-E-T30_paper

For every band file <run>_<band>.pt that all the runs have (e.g. 0to20dB, or 0to10dB + 10to20dB of fine-tuned runs),
it writes <folder of the first run>/<tag>/<tag>_<band>.pt (+ .mat, + README.txt). evaluate.py and compare.py then use
the ensemble like any other network. The members must use the same CS matrix.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --runs RUNS [RUNS ...]
                        run folders (at least two)
  --tag TAG             name of the ensemble folder, e.g. UTRR-E-T30_paper
  --out OUT             parent folder of the ensemble (default: that of the
                        first run)
```

## make_gmlamp_data.py

```
usage: make_gmlamp_data.py [-h] [--sv] [--deepmimo-ula DEEPMIMO_ULA]
                           [--deepmimo-upa DEEPMIMO_UPA] [--only ONLY]
                           [--out-root OUT_ROOT]

Make the four data sets of the GM-LAMP setting (paper reproduction), exactly the data the review used.

  python scripts/make_gmlamp_data.py --sv
  python scripts/make_gmlamp_data.py --deepmimo-ula H_ula_1.mat --deepmimo-upa H_upa.mat
  python scripts/make_gmlamp_data.py --sv --deepmimo-ula H_ula_1.mat --deepmimo-upa H_upa.mat     (all four)
  options: --out-root data (default)   --only SV_ULA,DeepMIMO_UPA

What is made (the GM-LAMP setting, configs/scenarios/sv_ula.yaml, sv_upa.yaml, deepmimo_ula.yaml, deepmimo_upa.yaml):
  SV_ULA, SV_UPA   GM-LAMP's channel generator (generate_channel.m, L = 3 paths, half-wavelength, lens DFT matrix),
                   training 80,000 (as GM-LAMP's generate_channel_data_for_SV_channel_model.m), validation 2,000,
                   test 2,000 (as GM-LAMP's Main.m: K = 2000); fixed seeds -> identical files every time
  DeepMIMO_ULA/UPA your raw DeepMIMO v1.3 channels (O1_28, BS 3, rows 1000-1300, 3 paths, ULA on the z axis /
                   UPA y-z; matlab/deepmimo_make_H.m), x = U0^H h, ||x||^2 = N (GM-LAMP's convention);
                   test = GM-LAMP's own CE_DeepMIMO test file (2,000), its users removed; training 50,000,
                   validation 2,000 drawn from the other 52,481 users
  measurements     as GM-LAMP's generate_measurement_data.py: y = A (x + n), CS matrix of GM-LAMP
                   (CSmatrix256128 for SV, CSmatrix_128256 for DeepMIMO); two bands 0-10 dB and 10-20 dB:
                   training split in 10 chunks with SNR ~ U(band), validation at 10 dB (GM-LAMP's validation SNR)
  test noise       not stored: evaluate.py adds it at 0, 2, ..., 20 dB with fixed seeds (same for every method)
At the end the data fingerprints are compared with the data of the review (status.py --data): 4 x OK expected.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --sv                  make SV_ULA and SV_UPA
  --deepmimo-ula DEEPMIMO_ULA
                        raw DeepMIMO ULA file (deepmimo_make_H(..., 'ULA'))
  --deepmimo-upa DEEPMIMO_UPA
                        raw DeepMIMO UPA file (deepmimo_make_H(..., 'UPA'))
  --only ONLY           comma list of SV_ULA, SV_UPA, DeepMIMO_ULA,
                        DeepMIMO_UPA
  --out-root OUT_ROOT
```

## make_scenario.py

```
usage: make_scenario.py [-h] --base BASE --name NAME [--n-train N_TRAIN]
                        [--n-val N_VAL] [--n-test N_TEST]
                        [--val-points VAL_POINTS] [--single-band]
                        [--val-random VAL_RANDOM]

Create a scenario variant (data sizes, validation SNRs) without touching the original files.

  python scripts/make_scenario.py --base sv_ula --name SV_ULA_150k --n-train 150000 --n-val 10000 --n-test 10000 --val-points 5
  python scripts/make_scenario.py --base sv_upa --name SV_UPA_valrange --val-points 5
  python scripts/make_scenario.py --base deepmimo_upa --name DeepMIMO_UPA_valrange --val-points 5
  python scripts/make_scenario.py --base sv_ula --name SV_ULA_fast --n-train 15000 --n-val 2000 --n-test 2000 --val-random 10

Writes configs/scenarios/<name lower-case>.yaml (inherits everything from the base file via _base)
with its own data_dir data/<name> and outputs in outputs/<name>, so the reproduction data stay as
they are. --val-points K replaces the single validation SNR of every band by K equally spaced SNRs
over the band's training range (e.g. 0, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10 dB); --val-random K draws K SNRs uniformly
at random in the band (seeded; validation chunk k gets SNR k, as genMeasurements does for training); training with --protocol gmlamp_best
then validates with the mean over these SNRs (in dB) and keeps the best weights.
SV: the first channels are the same as in the base data (same seeds), the sets are just longer.
DeepMIMO: sizes are limited by the users of H_*.mat (O1_28 rows 1000-1300: 54,481 users, 52,481
without GM-LAMP's test users); for more users generate more rows with matlab/deepmimo_make_H.m and
convert with --test random.
Next: generate_data.py (SV) or deepmimo_convert.py + generate_data.py --measurements-only (DeepMIMO)
with --scenario configs/scenarios/<name>.yaml.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --base BASE           sv_ula, sv_upa, deepmimo_ula, deepmimo_upa (or a yaml
                        path)
  --name NAME
  --n-train N_TRAIN
  --n-val N_VAL
  --n-test N_TEST
  --val-points VAL_POINTS
                        validation SNRs per band (equally spaced)
  --single-band         one network for the whole SNR range (e.g. 0-20 dB)
                        instead of the base bands
  --val-random VAL_RANDOM
                        validation SNRs per band drawn uniformly at random in
                        the band (seeded, like the training chunks)
```

## make_sv_measurements.py

```
usage: make_sv_measurements.py [-h] --scenario SCENARIO [--snr SNR [SNR ...]]
                               [--force] [--seed SEED] [--only {train,val}]
                               [--noise-model {colored,coloured,folded,white}]
                               [--snr-dist {chunks,fair}]
                               [--snr-step SNR_STEP]

Make the measurement files of a scenario from its channel files, like generate_SV_data.py / generate_measurement_data.py:
y = A (x + n), the K columns split into n_snr_chunks equal chunks, chunk k at SNR_k ~ U(lo, hi) dB, sigma^2 = 10^(-SNR/10).

  python scripts/make_sv_measurements.py --scenario configs/scenarios/sv_ula_user.yaml
  python scripts/make_sv_measurements.py --scenario configs/scenarios/sv_upa_user_2band.yaml
  python scripts/make_sv_measurements.py --scenario configs/scenarios/sv_upa.yaml --snr 0 5 10 15 20
  options: --snr <edges> (any SNR bands)  --force (overwrite existing files)   --seed 0   --only train|val
           --noise-model white   white files y = A x + w (<name>_white.mat): the colored file of the same draw with its
                                 noise whitened (made from the colored file when it exists; bsce/data/noise.py)
           --snr-dist fair [--snr-step 0.2]   (v26) every training column its own SNR, spread evenly over the band
                                 (<name>_fair.mat / _fair0p2.mat); validation over a range at equally spaced SNRs
                                 (<name>_fair.mat): the files train.py --snr-dist fair uses

For every band of the scenario:
  training   <data_dir>/<D>_<ARR>_training_<M>_measurements_<train_name or name>.mat   SNR ~ U(band.train)
  validation <data_dir>/<D>_<ARR>_validation_<M>_measurements_<val_name or name>.mat SNR ~ U(band.val_range)
             (band.val_range missing -> the band's val_snr points, one chunk each)
Existing files are kept (your SV_UPA_*_0to20dB / _1_11dB files are not touched). Each file also stores the SNR of
every column ('snr_db', needed by NF-LADMM in file mode); the chunk SNRs are in <file>.snr.json.
train.py makes missing files itself; this script is for making them ahead of time.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenario SCENARIO
  --snr SNR [SNR ...]   SNR band edges instead of the scenario's bands: 0 20
                        -> 0to20dB; 0 10 20 -> 0to10dB, 10to20dB
  --force
  --seed SEED
  --only {train,val}
  --noise-model {colored,coloured,folded,white}
                        colored y = A (x + n) (default: the scenario's) or
                        white y = A x + w
  --snr-dist {chunks,fair}
                        chunks (default, as before) or fair: one SNR per
                        training column, spread evenly over the band
  --snr-step SNR_STEP   with --snr-dist fair: the SNR grid step in dB
```

## promote_layer.py

```
usage: promote_layer.py [-h] --run RUN [RUN ...] --T T [T ...] [--force]

Turn the network saved after layer T of a deep run (--save-layers) into a normal T-layer run folder.

  %run scripts/promote_layer.py --run outputs/SV_UPA/LADMM-T12 --T 6
  %run scripts/promote_layer.py --run "outputs/*/LADMM-T12" --T 6          (every scenario at once)

With layer-wise training, the network saved when layer T is finished IS the network that a run with T layers trains
(same data, same seed, same protocol: the first T layers see exactly the same stages and minibatches; checked bit for
bit on the CPU). So after choosing the depth there is no need to retrain: this script writes

  outputs/<SCENARIO>/<name with -T12 replaced by -T6>/<name>_<band>.pt/.mat/_orig.mat, train_log.json, README.txt

which run_suite.py then finds ("trained, skipped") and continues with the fine-tune. Nothing is overwritten unless
--force is given.

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --run RUN [RUN ...]  deep run folder(s); patterns with * allowed
  --T T [T ...]        layer(s) to promote, e.g. 4 6
  --force
```

## rename_runs.py

```
usage: rename_runs.py [-h] [--outputs OUTPUTS [OUTPUTS ...]] [--apply]

Give the fine-tuned folders of bsce v23 and older the v24 names (dry run unless --apply).

  %run scripts/rename_runs.py              lists what would be renamed, changes nothing
  %run scripts/rename_runs.py --apply      renames

  v23 and older:  outputs/SV_UPA/LADMM-T6-ft/LADMM-T6-ft_0to10dB.pt
  v24:            outputs/SV_UPA/LADMM-T6_ft_0-10-20dB_20k/LADMM-T6_ft_0-10-20dB_20k_0to10dB.pt
The bands come from the old name (-ft = 0-10-20 dB, -ft0-5-10-15-20 = those edges), the iterations from the folder's
finetune_log.json; the rest of the name (_margin1, ...) is kept. Every file <old>_<band>.* is renamed, and the name in
finetune_log.json and README.txt is updated. A folder whose new name exists already, or without finetune_log.json (an
ensemble, a folder made by hand), is left as it is.
Comparisons made before keep the old names in their tables; compare.py run again shows the new ones.
--outputs outputs outputs_e4 ...   folders to look in (default: every outputs* folder of bsce)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --outputs OUTPUTS [OUTPUTS ...]
  --apply
```
