## run_suite.py

```
usage: run_suite.py [-h] --scenarios SCENARIOS [SCENARIOS ...]
                    [--methods METHODS [METHODS ...]]
                    [--protocol {ladmm_best,gmlamp_best,gmlamp,fair,e2e,paper}]
                    [--force-protocol] [--train-snr TRAIN_SNR [TRAIN_SNR ...]]
                    [--ft-snr FT_SNR [FT_SNR ...]] [--ft-iters FT_ITERS]
                    [--ft-patience FT_PATIENCE] [--save-layers]
                    [--warm-start {protocol,cold,warm,best}]
                    [--schedule {layerwise,e2e}] [--e2e-steps E2E_STEPS]
                    [--grad-clip GRAD_CLIP] [--margin MARGIN]
                    [--ft-margin FT_MARGIN] [--val-snr VAL_SNR [VAL_SNR ...]]
                    [--snr-chunks SNR_CHUNKS] [--snr-dist {chunks,fair}]
                    [--snr-step SNR_STEP]
                    [--noise-model {colored,coloured,folded,white}]
                    [--seed SEED] [--device DEVICE] [--out OUT]
                    [--set [SET ...]] [--ensemble [ENSEMBLE ...]] [--smoke]
                    [--dry-run]

Train (and fine-tune) any set of learned methods on any scenarios with ONE common protocol.

  %run scripts/run_suite.py --scenarios sv_upa --methods ladmm lamp gmlamp --device cuda
  %run scripts/run_suite.py --scenarios all --methods all --device cuda
  %run scripts/run_suite.py ... --dry-run                (print the commands, run nothing)

SCENARIOS  names in configs/scenarios (sv_ula, sv_upa, deepmimo_ula, deepmimo_upa, 3gpp_upa, 3gpp_ula, or any yaml path);
           'all' = the four GM-LAMP data sets (made by scripts/make_gmlamp_data.py); '3gpp' = 3gpp_upa and 3gpp_ula (made by
           scripts/make_3gpp_data.py); 'all 3gpp' = all six
METHODS    <key>[T]; the number is the number of layers, default = the method's paper depth:
             ladmm     LADMM (full 256x256 operator)        T = 6
             lamp      LAMP  (Borgerding; Wei-Hu-Dai)       T = 8
             gmlamp    GM-LAMP (Wei-Hu-Dai, K = 4)          T = 8
             lista     LISTA (complex)                      T = 16
             alista    ALISTA (analytic W)                  T = 16
             lvamp     LVAMP                                T = 6
             admmnet   ADMM-Net (THADMM-Net)                T = 15
             cadmm     complex ADMM-Net, untied M1/M2 (Johnston et al., TSP 2021)  T = 6   (v28; not in 'all': name it)
             gladmm    Graph-LADMM, analytic x-step: magnetic graph TV + energy gate; any combiner          T = 8
             gladmmf   Graph-LADMM with a free H_t per layer + graph gate (one combiner, like LADMM-F)        T = 6
             gladmmany Graph-LADMM trained on random combiners (any combiner / data set)                     T = 8
                       (v29; not in 'all': name them. v30: gladmm and gladmmany always get their own end-to-end
                       training, protocol paper, whatever --protocol is, unless --force-protocol; gladmmf takes
                       --protocol like every method)
             nfladmm   NF-LADMM-S (proposed, CNN denoiser)  T = 8
             nfladmmc  NF-LADMM-C (proposed, radial)        T = 8
             nfladmmsr NF-LADMM-SR (suggested: CNN denoiser + over-relaxed update + slope init 2)   T = 4
             utrr      UTRR (Wu-Cheng-Eldar-Cioffi, TCOM 2025; top-K 16 in the last layer) T = 30
                       (not in 'all': name it; with its own training: --protocol paper)
             ladmmat   LADMM + noise-adaptive soft threshold, blind noise level (median) per channel     T = 6
             ladmmatr  LADMM-AT with the noise level from the previous layer's whitened residual       T = 6
             ladmmatrd LADMM-ATR + a least-squares debias layer on a soft support (3 parameters)       T = 6
                       (v31.3; not in 'all': name them; full operator and training as ladmm)
           LADMM model options (--set, or a method row's own settings in the workbench), v28:
             model.threshold=adaptive|firm|gm   noise-adaptive shrinkage (blind noise level per channel)
             model.data_step=whitened           exact data step of the folded noise y = A (x + n)
             model.operator=analytic|analytic1  (A^T A + rho I)^-1 by SVD, 3 / 2 parameters per layer
             model.noise_level=residual         (v31.3, with adaptive|firm|gm) noise level from the previous residual
             model.debias=ls                    (v31.3) least-squares debias layer after the last layer
           e.g. ladmm4, lamp6, lista12.  'all' = every method at its default depth.
PROTOCOL   --protocol ladmm_best (default, the same for every method) | gmlamp_best | gmlamp | fair | e2e |
           paper (each method's own training settings)          -> configs/train/<name>_protocol.yaml
           (v30: except gladmm / gladmmany, which keep their own, protocol paper; --force-protocol to change)
SNR        --train-snr 0 20       band edges of the networks trained from scratch (default: one network 0-20 dB);
                                  '0 10 20' = two networks; 'scenario' = the scenario's own bands (GM-LAMP: 0-10 and
                                  10-20 dB, 10 SNR chunks, validation at 10 dB)
           --ft-snr 0 10 20       fine-tune the one network per band (default 0-10, 10-20); 'none' = no fine-tune
           --ft-iters 20000       fine-tune iterations per band
           --snr-dist fair        (v26) every training sample its own SNR, spread evenly over the band in random order,
                                  instead of the SNR chunks of the measurement files (the authors 10, ranges 100); the
                                  fine-tune minibatches spread evenly too; validation over a range at equally spaced
                                  SNRs. Suffix _fair (trained and fine-tuned folders); files <band>_fair.mat
           --snr-step 0.2         with --snr-dist fair: the SNRs on the grid lo, lo+0.2, ..., hi, equal counts (_fair0p2)
WARM START --warm-start protocol   (default) as the protocol says (ladmm_best / fair / e2e: cold; gmlamp, gmlamp_best:
                                  warm; paper: each method's own config, LAMP / GM-LAMP warm)
           --warm-start cold|warm  the same for every method (folder suffix _cold / _warm)
           --warm-start best      (v31.3) every layer-wise method trained twice, cold and warm (_cold / _warm), and the
                                  one with the better VALIDATION NMSE kept: outputs/<SCENARIO>/best_warm_start.json;
                                  compare.py --best leaves the other one out. Each method is then compared in its best
                                  configuration, chosen by one rule for all and never on the test set. Methods that train
                                  all layers together (end to end) have no new layer to initialise: trained once.
DEPTH      --save-layers          save the network after every layer (scripts/depth_snapshots.py plots the depth curve);
                                  v31.2: methods that train end to end in a mixed list train at full depth only
SCHEDULE   --schedule layerwise   (default) every method as its protocol says: layer by layer for ladmm_best / gmlamp /
                                  gmlamp_best / fair; the method's own schedule for paper; end to end for e2e
           --schedule e2e         ALL methods end to end: all layers trained together from the start, Adam with cosine
                                  decay lr -> 0.05 lr over --e2e-steps minibatches (default 30000), validation every
                                  500 steps, best validated state kept. lr, batch, loss, noise and precision stay those
                                  of --protocol. Folder suffix _e2e<steps>, e.g. LADMM-T6_e2e30k
CLIPPING   --grad-clip 1.0        clip the global gradient norm of EVERY method at 1.0, in training and in the fine-tune
                                  (folder suffix _clip1). --grad-clip none: no clipping for every method, also where
                                  the method's own config clips (--protocol paper / e2e; suffix _noclip).
                                  Default (option not given): as now. The common protocols clip nobody; e2e clips
                                  everybody at 1.0; paper keeps each method's own setting.
NOISE      --noise-model white    white measurement noise y = A x + w (same mean noise power) instead of the colored
                                  y = A (x + n) of GM-LAMP (default). Runs go to outputs/<SCENARIO>_white/ with the same
                                  folder names, so the two noise models can be compared run by run; the white files are
                                  the colored ones with the same noise draw whitened (bsce/data/noise.py)
ENSEMBLE   --ensemble ladmm6 ladmm8  (v28, off by default) after the training, average the final networks of these
                                  methods (fine-tuned if --ft-snr, else trained; the names this command gives them) into
                                  one network per band: outputs/<SCENARIO>/ENS-LADMM-T6+LADMM-T8[_<shared suffix>]/
                                  (scripts/make_ensemble.py; xhat = mean of the members). The methods need not be in
                                  --methods: the ensemble is made as soon as all members exist (with --split per method,
                                  the last command makes it), and skipped when it exists.
OTHER      --seed 0   --device auto|cuda|cpu   --out outputs   --set train.lr=1e-4 ... (passed to train.py)
           --smoke                tiny data and budget (checks the pipeline on the CPU in minutes)

Folder names (outputs/<SCENARIO>/<name>/), built only from the choices, so every computer makes the same names:
  <METHOD>-T<T>[_<protocol>][_tr<edges>][_<override>][_s<seed>]   trained network(s), e.g. LADMM-T6,
                                                         LAMP-T8_paper_trscenario, LADMM-T6_restore-best-true
  <that>_ft_<edges>dB_<iterations>[_margin<M>]          fine-tuned per band, next to it: LADMM-T6_ft_0-10-20dB_20k,
                                                         LADMM-T6_ft_0-5-10-15-20dB_20k (files <folder>_<band>.pt)
  (_<protocol> only when it is not ladmm_best; _tr only when the training range is not 0-20 dB; every --set override
   is added too, e.g. _restore-best-true. Fine-tunes of v23 and older, <that>-ft[<edges>], are still found and skipped;
   scripts/rename_runs.py gives them the new names.)
Resume: an interrupted training or fine-tune continues from its last checkpoint when the same command is run again
  (inside a stage every 10 minutes; finished bands are kept), and gives exactly the networks of an uninterrupted run.
Every run is independent (own seed, own subprocess, data files made deterministically), so methods can be split
over several commands or computers: e.g. '--methods lamp gmlamp' on one PC and '--methods ladmm ladmm4' on another
give the same networks as one command with all four. A step whose files exist is skipped; the same command
continues an interrupted suite (train.py also resumes inside a run from its checkpoint).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenarios SCENARIOS [SCENARIOS ...]
  --methods METHODS [METHODS ...]
  --protocol {ladmm_best,gmlamp_best,gmlamp,fair,e2e,paper}
  --force-protocol      v30: train every method with --protocol, the analytic
                        Graph-LADMM (gladmm, gladmmany) included (default:
                        they keep their own end-to-end training, protocol
                        paper)
  --train-snr TRAIN_SNR [TRAIN_SNR ...]
  --ft-snr FT_SNR [FT_SNR ...]
  --ft-iters FT_ITERS
  --ft-patience FT_PATIENCE
                        fine-tune early stop: steps without a gain of 0.01 dB
                        before the learning rate (then the band) ends; default
                        4000 (finetune_bands.py); 0 = always the whole --ft-
                        iters (folder suffix _pat0)
  --save-layers
  --warm-start {protocol,cold,warm,best}
                        v31.3: initialise each new layer from the trained
                        previous one? protocol (default): as the protocol
                        says; cold / warm: for every method; best: both, the
                        better one on validation kept
  --schedule {layerwise,e2e}
                        layerwise (default): as the protocol says; e2e: every
                        method end to end
  --e2e-steps E2E_STEPS
                        minibatches of --schedule e2e (default 30000)
  --grad-clip GRAD_CLIP
                        gradient-norm clip for every method (training + fine-
                        tune), e.g. 1.0; 'none' = no clipping; default: as now
  --margin MARGIN       edge margin (dB) of the training bands: each band
                        trained on [lo-M, hi+M], used on [lo, hi]; folder
                        suffix _margin<M> (default 0, as the authors)
  --ft-margin FT_MARGIN
                        edge margin (dB) of the fine-tune bands; fine-tune
                        folder suffix _margin<M> (default 0)
  --val-snr VAL_SNR [VAL_SNR ...]
                        validation noise of training and fine-tune: 'range' =
                        SNR ~ U(band), or SNRs, e.g. '10' (the authors).
                        Default: as now (authors' bands: 10 dB; --train-snr
                        ranges and fine-tune: the range). Folder suffix
                        _valrange / _val10
  --snr-chunks SNR_CHUNKS
                        SNR chunks of the training measurement files (the
                        authors 10; ranges 100); suffix _c<N>
  --snr-dist {chunks,fair}
                        training SNRs: chunks (default, as before) or fair =
                        every sample its own SNR, spread evenly over the band
                        (training files, online noise, fine-tune); suffix
                        _fair
  --snr-step SNR_STEP   with --snr-dist fair: SNRs on the grid lo, lo+STEP,
                        ..., hi dB (e.g. 0.2); suffix _fair<step>
  --noise-model {colored,coloured,folded,white}
                        measurement noise: colored y = A (x + n) (default: the
                        scenario's noise_model, else colored) or white y = A x
                        + w; white runs go to outputs/<SCENARIO>_white/
  --seed SEED
  --device DEVICE
  --out OUT
  --set [SET ...]
  --ensemble [ENSEMBLE ...]
                        v28: after training, average the final networks of
                        these methods (e.g. ladmm6 ladmm8) into one ensemble
                        per scenario (off by default)
  --smoke
  --dry-run
```

## runs.py

```
usage: runs.py [-h] [--outputs OUTPUTS [OUTPUTS ...]]
               [--scenario [SCENARIO ...]] [--no-write]

Every trained and fine-tuned network at a glance: what it is, whether it is finished, and where an interrupted one
will resume. Writes outputs/RUNS.md and outputs/RUNS.csv.

  %run scripts/runs.py                       every outputs/<SCENARIO>/<run>/
  %run scripts/runs.py --scenario SV_UPA     one scenario folder (also SV_UPA_white, ...)
  %run scripts/runs.py --outputs outputs outputs_e4 --no-write

Columns: run folder, kind (trained / fine-tuned from <source> / published / other), method and layers, parameters,
bands present (of those expected), state, best validation NMSE per band (dB), last change.
State:
  done                    every expected band network is there
  resumable: <where>      interrupted; the same command continues from the checkpoint (stage and iteration shown)
  incomplete              some band networks are missing and there is no checkpoint (the command starts them again)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --outputs OUTPUTS [OUTPUTS ...]
  --scenario [SCENARIO ...]
                        scenario folders (names or prefixes), e.g. SV_UPA
  --no-write
```

## select_depth.py

```
usage: select_depth.py [-h] --scenario SCENARIO --train TRAIN [TRAIN ...]
                       [--T T [T ...]] [--snr SNR [SNR ...]]
                       [--noise {file,online}] [--protocol PROTOCOL]
                       [--device DEVICE] [--set [SET ...]] [--tol TOL]
                       [--retrain] [--runs-only] [--smoke]
                       [--runs-root RUNS_ROOT] [--out OUT]

Choose the number of layers T of one or several methods (e.g. LADMM and NF-LADMM) on the validation set.

  python scripts/select_depth.py --scenario configs/scenarios/sv_upa.yaml --snr 0 20 --T 2 4 6 8 10 12          --train configs/train/ladmm_best.yaml configs/train/nfladmm_s.yaml --device cuda
  options: --tol 0.1          recommended T = smallest T within tol dB of the best T, in every band
           --protocol gmlamp  (passed to train.py)   --noise online|file   --snr <edges> (any SNR bands)
           --set train.steps=10000 ...                (passed to train.py for every config)
           --retrain          train again even if the run exists      --out outputs/depth_select
           --runs-only        do not train; read the existing runs

How T is measured, per training schedule:
  * layer-wise (schedule borgerding: LAMP, GM-LAMP, LADMM): one run with T = max(--T). The validation NMSE of every
    depth t is logged when layer t is finished (with its refinements), so one run gives the whole curve; the prefixes
    of the final network are not used (they are retuned later). Run folder <tag>-T<max>.
  * end to end (schedule steps / end2end: NF-LADMM): one run per T (folders <tag>-T<t>), final validation NMSE.
Each method uses its own validation set (the one its training uses); the chosen T is then trained/evaluated as usual.
Writes <out>/<scenario>/depth_select.png (values printed), depth_select.csv, depth_select.json.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenario SCENARIO
  --train TRAIN [TRAIN ...]
                        train configs (one curve each)
  --T T [T ...]
  --snr SNR [SNR ...]
  --noise {file,online}
  --protocol PROTOCOL
  --device DEVICE
  --set [SET ...]
  --tol TOL
  --retrain
  --runs-only
  --smoke               tiny CPU check (train.py --smoke)
  --runs-root RUNS_ROOT
  --out OUT
```

## sionna_make_H.py

```
usage: sionna_make_H.py [-h] --array {UPA,ULA_Y,ULA} [--n N] --out OUT
                        [--scenario {umi,umi_los,umi_nlos}]
                        [--spec {16.1,19.2}] [--fc FC]
                        [--element {38.901,omni}] [--isd ISD] [--d-min D_MIN]
                        [--h-bs H_BS] [--h-ut H_UT] [--indoor INDOOR]
                        [--drop-users DROP_USERS] [--part-users PART_USERS]
                        [--seed SEED] [--parts PARTS] [--device DEVICE]
                        [--threads THREADS]

Raw 3GPP TR 38.901 channels with Sionna (the standard's procedure as written), saved in parts as H (N x K complex).

  python scripts/sionna_make_H.py --array UPA   --n 100000 --out data/raw3gpp/H_3gpp_upa
  python scripts/sionna_make_H.py --array ULA_Y --n 100000 --out data/raw3gpp/H_3gpp_ulay
  then (bsce environment):
  python scripts/make_dataset.py --dataset 3GPP --array UPA --input "data/raw3gpp/H_3gpp_upa_part*.mat" ...

Needs Sionna 2.2 without its ray tracer, best in its own environment (PyTorch >= 2.9.1; the CPU build is enough):
  conda create -n sionna python=3.12 -y  &  conda activate sionna  &  pip install sionna-no-rt==2.2.0 scipy
This script imports only numpy, scipy, torch and sionna (no bsce module), so it runs in that environment.

The setting is that of matlab/quadriga_make_H.m and docs/3GPP_DATASET.md:
  model     38.901 UMi street canyon (sionna.phy.channel.tr38901.UMi), tables of --spec 16.1 (default) or 19.2;
            LOS/NLOS per user by Table 7.4.2-1 (--scenario umi), or all LOS / all NLOS (umi_los, umi_nlos)
  carrier   --fc 28e9 (= DeepMIMO O1_28)
  BS        height 10 m at the origin, boresight +x, single-polarised (V) panel with the 38.901 element of Table 7.3-1
            (--element omni = isotropic), lambda/2: UPA 16 x 16 (y-z), ULA_Y 1 x 256 (y), ULA 256 x 1 (z)
  UE        one isotropic antenna, 1.5 m, outdoor (--indoor = fraction of O2I users, low-loss model)
  users     uniform in the 120-degree hexagonal sector cell of the site (ISD 200 m), 2-D distance >= 10 m
  channel   narrowband at the carrier: h = sum of the path coefficients; plane waves; no path loss and no shadowing
            here (bsce normalises ||x||^2 = N per channel anyway)
Element order of H: horizontal (y) index slow, vertical (z) index fast, as quadriga_make_H.m.
Drops of --drop-users users (new topology and LSPs per drop); drop d uses the seed (--seed, d), so any part can be made
alone (--parts 1-10 here, 11-20 on another computer). Existing parts made with the same settings are kept (resume).

Saved per part (<out>_part001.mat, ...): H (N x Kp), loc (Kp x 3), los, indoor, drop (Kp x 1),
lsp (Kp x 7: DS [s], ASD, ASA, ZSD, ZSA [deg], K-factor [dB], SF [dB], as drawn by Sionna), lsp_real (NaN), lsp_names,
params (the settings; num_ant_x/y/z as matlab/deepmimo_make_H.m).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --array {UPA,ULA_Y,ULA}
  --n N
  --out OUT             prefix of the part files, e.g. data/raw3gpp/H_3gpp_upa
  --scenario {umi,umi_los,umi_nlos}
  --spec {16.1,19.2}    38.901 tables: 16.1 (as QuaDRiGa 2.8.1) or 19.2 (the
                        Rel-19 update; Sionna's own default)
  --fc FC
  --element {38.901,omni}
  --isd ISD
  --d-min D_MIN
  --h-bs H_BS
  --h-ut H_UT
  --indoor INDOOR       fraction of O2I users (38.901 calibration: 0.8)
  --drop-users DROP_USERS
  --part-users PART_USERS
  --seed SEED
  --parts PARTS         e.g. 1-10 or '1 3 5' (default: all)
  --device DEVICE       cpu or cuda
  --threads THREADS     CPU threads for PyTorch (0 = PyTorch's default)
```

## speed_test.py

```
usage: speed_test.py [-h] [--scenario SCENARIO]
                     [--configs CONFIGS [CONFIGS ...]] [--iters ITERS]
                     [--devices DEVICES [DEVICES ...]]

Short timed trainings to choose device and precision before the long runs.

  python scripts/speed_test.py                     (SV_ULA, band 0to10dB, ~5-15 min in total)
  python scripts/speed_test.py --iters 500 --configs gmlamp_spread ladmm_original

For each config x device (cuda, cpu) x precision (float64, float32) a 2-layer network is trained
for a fixed number of iterations per stage (no early stop), with --protocol gmlamp, and the wall
time is recorded. Writes outputs/speed_test.json / .csv / .png and prints the fastest setting per
method. The precision only changes speed and round-off; the protocol is the same.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenario SCENARIO
  --configs CONFIGS [CONFIGS ...]
  --iters ITERS
  --devices DEVICES [DEVICES ...]
```

## train.py

```
usage: train.py [-h] --scenario SCENARIO [--method METHOD] [--train TRAIN]
                [--protocol {original,paper,fair,gmlamp,gmlamp_best,ladmm_best,e2e}]
                [--bands BANDS] [--device DEVICE] [--out OUT] [--tag TAG]
                [--save-layers] [--smoke] [--seed SEED] [--snr SNR [SNR ...]]
                [--margin MARGIN] [--val-snr VAL_SNR [VAL_SNR ...]]
                [--snr-chunks SNR_CHUNKS] [--snr-dist {chunks,fair}]
                [--snr-step SNR_STEP] [--noise {file,online}]
                [--noise-model {colored,coloured,folded,white}]
                [--set [SET ...]]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenario SCENARIO   a name (sv_upa, deepmimo_ula, 3gpp_upa, ...) or a yaml
                        path
  --method METHOD       instead of --train: <key><layers> as in run_suite.py,
                        e.g. ladmm6, lamp8, nfladmmsr4 (defaults then as
                        run_suite.py: --protocol ladmm_best, --snr 0 20,
                        folder <METHOD>-T<T>[_options])
  --train TRAIN         a train config yaml (configs/train/...), instead of
                        --method
  --protocol {original,paper,fair,gmlamp,gmlamp_best,ladmm_best,e2e}
                        default: ladmm_best with --method, original with
                        --train. original (= paper): each method's own script;
                        fair: configs/train/fair_protocol.yaml; gmlamp: GM-
                        LAMP's training procedure for every method
                        (configs/train/gmlamp_protocol.yaml); gmlamp_best: the
                        same + best validated weights restored + validation
                        averaged over the validation SNRs
                        (configs/train/gmlamp_best_protocol.yaml); ladmm_best:
                        the protocol of the user's best SV UPA 0-20 dB LADMM,
                        untitled2.py (configs/train/ladmm_best_protocol.yaml);
                        e2e: all layers trained together end to end
                        (configs/train/e2e_protocol.yaml)
  --bands BANDS
  --device DEVICE
  --out OUT
  --tag TAG
  --save-layers         save the network when each layer is finished:
                        <tag>/layers/T<t>_<tag>_<band>.pt/.mat (a real t-layer
                        estimator at that moment; test depth curve:
                        scripts/depth_snapshots.py)
  --smoke
  --seed SEED           training seed (init + minibatches); seed k > 0 adds
                        _s<k> to the folder name
  --snr SNR [SNR ...]   SNR band edges in dB, replacing the scenario's bands:
                        '--snr 0 20' = one network for 0-20 dB (the default
                        with --method), '--snr 0 10 20' = two networks (0-10,
                        10-20), '--snr -5 30' ...; 'scenario' = the scenario's
                        own bands (the default with --train)
  --margin MARGIN       edge margin in dB: each band is trained on [lo - M, hi
                        + M] and used for [lo, hi], so its edges are trained
                        like its middle (default 0 = as the authors).
                        Validation stays on [lo, hi]
  --val-snr VAL_SNR [VAL_SNR ...]
                        validation noise: 'range' = SNR ~ U(band) (fixed), or
                        SNRs in dB, e.g. '10' (the authors: 10 dB for both
                        bands). Default: as the bands define it (scenario
                        bands: their val_snr; --snr bands: range)
  --snr-chunks SNR_CHUNKS
                        SNR chunks of the training measurement file (the
                        authors 10; --snr bands 100)
  --snr-dist {chunks,fair}
                        how the training SNRs cover a band: chunks (default,
                        as before: the training file in SNR chunks, one random
                        SNR each; online noise i.i.d. U(band)); fair: every
                        sample its own SNR, spread evenly over the band in
                        random order (files <band>_fair.mat, folder suffix
                        _fair); validation over a range at equally spaced SNRs
  --snr-step SNR_STEP   with --snr-dist fair: the SNRs on the grid lo,
                        lo+STEP, ..., hi dB, every value equally often (e.g.
                        0.2 -> 0, 0.2, ..., 20); default: continuous
  --noise {file,online}
                        file: measurement files (made automatically if
                        missing); online: fresh noise every minibatch, SNR ~
                        U(band) per sample, fixed generated validation set (=
                        --set train.noise=...)
  --noise-model {colored,coloured,folded,white}
                        measurement noise: colored = y = A (x + n) (GM-LAMP's
                        model, default) or white = y = A x + w with the same
                        mean noise power (bsce/data/noise.py). Default: the
                        scenario's noise_model
  --set [SET ...]
```

## tune_classical.py

```
usage: tune_classical.py [-h] --scenario SCENARIO [--snr [SNR ...]]
                         [--n-val N_VAL] [--methods METHODS] [--smoke]
                         [--out OUT]
                         [--noise-model {colored,coloured,folded,white}]

Tune the classical l1 ADMM and graph-reweighted l1 (v31) per test SNR on validation channels, for evaluate.py.

  %run scripts/tune_classical.py --scenario configs/scenarios/sv_upa.yaml
  %run scripts/evaluate.py --scenario configs/scenarios/sv_upa.yaml --runs outputs/SV_UPA --classical amp,l1,grwl1        --classical-params results/classical_params_SV_UPA.json

Per test SNR of the scenario (as the uploaded graph_reweighted_l1 package tunes, with the true SNR):
  l1     lam on 13 log points 10^-2.5 .. 10^0.5, then 0.65x and 1.5x the best;
  grwl1  lam_rw in {0.5, 1, 2, 3} x lam_l1 and eps in {0.05, 0.2, 0.6}; round 0 + 2 reweighted rounds.
Every solve is 300 ADMM iterations with rho = 1 (bsce.classical.l1_admm / grwl1). Validation: the first --n-val
channels of <data>/<scenario>_validation_channel.mat, noise rng NumpyMatlabRNG(seed + 9000 + i) (i = SNR index; the test
noise of evaluate.py uses seed + 1000 + i). Writes a JSON {snr: {lam_l1, val_l1_db, lam_rw, eps, val_rw_db}}.
About 2-3 min per SNR on one CPU core with 300 channels.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenario SCENARIO
  --snr [SNR ...]       test SNRs to tune (default: the scenario's)
  --n-val N_VAL
  --methods METHODS
  --smoke
  --out OUT             default results/classical_params_<SCENARIO>.json
                        (_white.json for white)
  --noise-model {colored,coloured,folded,white}
                        validation noise (v31.3): tune for the noise model the
                        comparison uses
```

## utrr_reproduce.py

```
usage: utrr_reproduce.py [-h] [--snr SNR] [--K K [K ...]] [--T T] [--bn BN]
                         [--ntrain NTRAIN] [--epochs EPOCHS]
                         [--patience PATIENCE] [--lrs LRS [LRS ...]]
                         [--batch BATCH] [--seed SEED] [--device DEVICE]
                         [--data DATA] [--out OUT]

Reproduce UTRR's Table II (Wu, Cheng, Eldar, Cioffi, IEEE TCOM 2025) in the paper's OWN setting, before UTRR is
compared with the other methods in bsce's setting.

The paper's setting differs from bsce's (= GM-LAMP's) in one point: the noise is added AFTER the combiner,
z = Phi h + n, with SNR = ||Phi h||^2 / ||n||^2 (bsce: y = A (x + n)). Everything else is bsce's SV ULA data set
(GM-LAMP's generator, 80,000 / 2,000 / 2,000 channels, M = 128, the CS matrix of GM-LAMP). One model per SNR and top-K,
trained as Sec. V-A: Adam, loss E||x - xhat||^2, batch 128 real samples, learning rates 0.005 -> 0.001 -> 0.0005 ->
0.0002 -> 0.0001, early stopping after 10 epochs without improvement per rate, at most 300 epochs, best weights kept.

  %run scripts/utrr_reproduce.py --snr 20 --K 16 --device cuda                 one model (Table II: -26.93 dB)
  %run scripts/utrr_reproduce.py --snr 20 --K 0 16 64 256 --device cuda        the four models, then UTRR-E (-30.18 dB)
  %run scripts/utrr_reproduce.py --snr 10 --K 0 16 64 256 --device cuda        Table II at 10 dB (-18.92 / -22.06 dB)
  options: --bn 1 (the batch normalisation of Fig. 6)  --ntrain 20000 (a shorter check)  --epochs 300  --patience 10

A stopped run resumes from its last epoch (results/utrr_reproduce/<tag>.ckpt.pt). Results: results/utrr_reproduce/
<tag>.json (validation per epoch, test NMSE), <tag>.pt, and table.md / table_2.png with every model and the ensemble.
```
